To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

active, constructive, interactive, and passive activities can be distinguished by overt activities and underlying processes, and that the most powerful learning activities are interactive, followed by constructive, followed by active.

active, constructive, interactive activities are different from each other and that interactive activities are more likely than constructive ones, which in turn are more likely than active activities, to lead to learning.

(1) Active, constructive, interactive, and passive are four different kinds of overt activity that can be observed in learning situations; (2) The four activities can be ordered according to the extent to which they promote deep learning; (3) Interactive activities are most likely better than constructive activities; (4) Constructive activities are most likely more effective than active activities; (5) Active activities are most likely superior to passive activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to differentiate learning activities and how to understand learning processes.
how learning activities are defined, how learning processes are inferred, and how learning outcomes might be measured.
the question, What are active, constructive, or interactive learning activities?

active-constructive-interactive activities are better than passive ones, and interactive ones are better than constructive ones, and constructive activities are better than active ones.
active-constructive-interactive activities are better than passive ones, but not all active-constructive activities are better than active-interactive ones.
the most effective learning activities are active-constructive-interactive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the framework can help to differentiate active, interactive, and constructive in terms of observable learning activities and underlying learning mechanisms.
active, constructive, interactive are distinct terms that can be operationalized in terms of overt manifestations and learning processes.
active, constructive, interactive, and passive activities are different ways of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three terms should not be used interchangeably and that each term has a specific definition and a specific meaning.
active, constructive, interactive, and passive activities are not just labels that we use to describe activities.
active, constructive, or interactive activities should not be used as synonyms.
